# Regimes: where omnibias wins, ties and loses

<!-- Generated by scripts/build_regime_guide.py from docs/benchmarks/full_scope.json. Do not edit; run the script. -->

This page is a view of [`full_scope.json`](benchmarks/full_scope.json), the matrix of every measured cell against every baseline (8,794 cells; 6,980 against independent baselines). It says what was measured, by regime, with the cells that lose next to the cells that win. It does not choose a program for your problem: [`explain()` and `mode="find"`](operator-planner.md#planning-for-training) do, on your shape and device.

**Reading a cell.** The ratio is baseline time over omnibias time; each cell carries a 95 % interval and the verdict reads the interval: `big win` when the lower bound is at least 2, `win` when it is above 1, `parity` when the interval contains 1, `loss` when the upper bound is below 1 (the baseline is faster with confidence), `incomplete` when the record has no qualified baseline for the cell (the baseline failed, was refused or did not qualify; that is not a slow baseline and not a win). Cells are one operator at one configuration against one baseline. A regime is the range of `D`, `H`, depth, order, batch and grid size the cells of a row cover, read from the cell label; it is a bounding range, not a guarantee between its ends. Protocol, intervals and every row: [performance evidence](performance.md#full-scope-matrix).

**Reading a baseline.** An independent baseline is another package or a textbook method. A generic engine fed omnibias's own projection shares that projection. A row against omnibias's own variants or a hand-written closed form compares two omnibias programs on the same XLA; a loss there names the variant that won and says nothing about other packages. Endpoints are as recorded: the device time of a captured program, an eager call, value-and-gradient, a solve to tolerance, or time to a target error with or without compilation.

Overall: 4,240 big wins, 2,186 wins, 1,066 at parity, 653 losses and 649 incomplete cells in 8,794.
